findings.evidence: Digest for dbff837f reports 'removed units (463, showing 40)'. All 40 shown items resolve: to section or para rows that fixer-rules allows (accepted drops, not-lost, redistributed, intended-change), or to restored content in references/text-memes.md, references/blog-posts.md and references/image-memes.md. The other 423 units could not be checked from the digest.
findings.fix: Re-run the removal check with the full digest (no cut) and confirm that each of the 423 unshown units has a valid row in docs/audit/recovery/meme-factory/record.md or is present in a named destination. Restore any unexplained unit into references/, or add a row for it.

findings.evidence: Step 4: 'First answer three questions. Who will see it: team Slack, a PR, or a public post? Who is the butt of the joke... Then name the contrast and write the payoff (last line) first, then the setup.'
findings.fix: The model already knows this audience and joke-craft advice; it only needs a reminder. Shorten it to one line that keeps the non-obvious parts (never a named teammate or customer; the ~30 and ~20 character limits per line) and leave the rest of the step as it is.

findings.evidence: Step 5 is one dense paragraph. It mixes the caption-count decision ('If the count differs, switch to a template ... only when the user named no template; otherwise stop and ask'), the full CLI usage line, the apostrophe quoting rule and the no-Python fallback.
findings.fix: Split step 5 into lettered sub-steps: (a) compare the caption count with `lines` and decide whether to switch templates or ask; (b) run the CLI line; (c) quote apostrophes; (d) no Python: go to Hand-built URLs. Keep every rule and only change the layout.

findings.evidence: 'The 15 named formats with samples and tips, and the Markdown techniques behind them, are in `text-memes.md`.' The greentext fence rule appears both here and in text-memes.md under 'Building blocks', so a named-format request reads two files that partly repeat each other.
findings.fix: In text-memes.md, keep a single pointer to the fence rule in markdown-memes-guide.md and drop the restated rule. Or state in SKILL.md step 1 that markdown-memes-guide.md is the only required read for greentext, copypasta and ASCII. Remove nothing else.

findings.evidence: 'States or shows that the captions were checked for sensitive content ... before the URL was built'. The sensitive-content assertions in casual-meme, precise-meme and slash-invocation pass on boilerplate even when the captions held nothing to redact.
findings.fix: Make these checks verifiable: put a sensitive token in the prompt of one of these evals (for example a hostname) and assert that it is missing from the URL, as the sensitive-caption eval already does. Keep the existing assertions.

findings.evidence: 'Invoked as `/meme-factory <template> <caption>...`: ... check the ID and line count as in step 3, then continue at step 5.' Step 3 only says to pick a template and check that the joke fits. The procedure for a caption count that differs from `lines` (switch only when no template was named, otherwise ask) is in step 5, so this branch points to the wrong step for that check.
findings.fix: Change the line to: 'Invoked as `/meme-factory <template> <caption>...`: take the template ID and the raw captions from the arguments, run step 2 on them first, look the ID up in the Templates table or the live catalog (never guess it), then continue at step 5, whose line-count check applies; the user named the template, so ask rather than switch.'
